newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 18.81 pct. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 18.81 pct. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects yield on six-month TEMs in headline and first paragraph from 21.26 percent.)
Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 257 basis points to 18.81 percent in Monday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.
The Central Bank said it sold 62.47 billion bolivars of 179-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 16.26 percent coupon for a price of 98.84 pct.
The total offering was for 70 billion bolivars.
At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 16.24 percent.

The bank also sold 10.55 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 16.58 percent coupon at a price of 97.95 percent and 10.69 billion bolivars of 360-day notes with a 16.92 percent coupon at an average price of 96.42 percent.

Yields for these notes rose 266 basis points to 19.73 percent for the 269-day bills, and 249 basis points to 21.26 percent for the 360-day TEMs. Fifteen billion bolivar of notes were offered at each maturity.
TEM bills are the Central Bank's principal monetary policy tool, used to restrict liquidity and set wider interest rates.
